hints: Look carefully at where X sits in the Venn diagram. It is in the very centre, so what three features must that structure have at the same time?
Compare the walls of the trachea, bronchus and bronchiole. Which ones are supported by cartilage and lined by mucus-secreting goblet cells plus cilia?
walkthrough:
**Read what X means**

Great start, let's decode the diagram together. X is the overlap of all three circles.

So a structure at X must have ciliated epithelium AND goblet cells AND cartilage all together.

**Recall the airway walls**

Now think down the airways from large to small. The trachea has C-shaped cartilage rings, ciliated epithelium and many goblet cells for mucus.

The bronchus (plural bronchi) is very similar, it still has cartilage plates, ciliated epithelium and goblet cells.

**Check the bronchiole**

The bronchiole is much narrower and its wall is different. It has ciliated epithelium and smooth muscle, but no cartilage to hold it open and no goblet cells.

So the bronchiole cannot sit in the centre where all three features overlap. Only 2 and 3 fit, which is option D.

options.A: Incorrect, because 1 is wrong. The bronchiole lacks cartilage and goblet cells, so it cannot have all three features at X.
options.B: Incorrect, because 1 is wrong. The bronchiole has no cartilage, so it does not belong at X even though the trachea (2) does.
options.C: Incorrect, because 1 is wrong. The bronchus (3) does belong at X, but the bronchiole (1) does not due to missing cartilage.
options.D: Correct and well done. Both trachea (2) and bronchus (3) have ciliated epithelium, goblet cells and cartilage, so they fit perfectly at X.
